books.section: Topic 4.7 Expanding Democracy, A. Participatory Democracy and an Expanding Electorate

stimulus.text: Paraphrase of Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 6, Topic 4.7 A: Rhode Island held onto property qualifications for voting longer than any other state. In a state with a growing class of propertyless industrial wageworkers, resentment was widespread. In 1841, democratic reformers organized a People's Convention, which wrote a new, more democratic state constitution. The reformers held an unsanctioned statewide referendum on their constitution, which passed overwhelmingly. They then tried to put the new constitution into effect and inaugurate a new governor, Thomas Dorr. None of these moves had official state approval; they were seen as an extralegal rebellion. President Tyler promised federal support and sent an observer, but no federal troops were sent. Dorr was briefly imprisoned, and the state militia quickly put the rebellion down.
stimulus.source_note: Secondary text: paraphrase of Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 6, Topic 4.7 A. Paraphrased, not quoted.

stem: The People's Convention and its referendum show that the reformers

options.text: had the federal government's approval for their new constitution
options.misconception: Their moves had no official approval, which is why they were called a rebellion.

options.text: were mostly wealthy landowners defending their own property
options.misconception: The reformers spoke for propertyless workers, the very people the old rule shut out.

wanted to keep the property qualification for voting in place
options.misconception: They wrote a new constitution precisely to get rid of it.

rationales.A: Their moves had no official approval at all.
rationales.B: The reformers spoke for propertyless workers, not landowners.
rationales.C: They wrote their own constitution and put it to a statewide vote, asking the people, not the legislature, to make it law.
rationales.D: Their new constitution was written to end the property rule.
rationales.general:
1. Name what they did. They held a People's Convention, wrote a constitution, and held a referendum on it.
2. Ask what they skipped. None of it had official state approval.
3. Name the claim. An overwhelming vote, they said, made their constitution legitimate.
Background: The referendum passed overwhelmingly, yet the old government called the whole effort an extralegal rebellion.
Remember: reformers who cannot win inside the rules sometimes ask the people to bless new ones.
